usage.notes: Treat Medplum as an optional FHIR backend/gateway rather than a mandatory Panacea dependency. Hosted Medplum currently exposes a FHIR R4 API. A self-hosted or hosted deployment still requires authenticated network boundaries; Panacea must remain usable for local/reference features when no Medplum connection exists.

license.scope: The medplum/medplum open-source repository is Apache-2.0 licensed. This license covers the software, not hosted-service subscriptions, patient data, third-party terminology content, external integrations or separate commercial agreements.
license.notes: Keep open-source licensing separate from hosted Medplum terms, data-processing agreements, deployment security, and any third-party service or terminology licenses.

validation.notes: Medplum is clinical-data infrastructure. Successful storage, retrieval or FHIR conformance does not validate the medical correctness of observations, diagnoses, medications, decision support or derived Panacea outputs.

provenance.authority: Medplum / Orangebot, Inc. and open-source contributors
provenance.notes: Preserve source project/server, FHIR R4 resourceType/id/meta.versionId, canonical profiles and audit context. Do not erase the distinction between a resource retrieved from Medplum and a locally derived Panacea representation.

adapter.notes: Planned flow: authenticated FHIR R4 endpoint -> SMART/OAuth and access-policy gate -> version/profile validation -> PanaceaFHIRGateway -> PanaceaHealthResource. Never store client secrets in the browser, public repository or localStorage. Prefer authorization-code/SMART flows for user-facing access and least-privilege scoped service credentials for backend tasks.

trust.notes: Scores describe infrastructure suitability, not biomedical evidence quality. Deployment architecture, access policies and hosted-service configuration materially affect operational trust.
